rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲣⲟⲕ/ϩⲣⲁϫ 'be calm, still.' Used here in the Manichaean death-vision: the Form of Light stills the dying elect 'with the kiss and her stillness, away from the fear of the demons.' The pair ⲡⲉⲥⲍⲣⲁⲕ (her stillness) vs. ⲧⲍⲣⲧⲉ (their fear) is correspondential — stillness expels fear at the moment of death.

Compound: ⲣⲁϩ- (Lyc reflex of ⲣⲉϥ- 'one who does') + ⲥⲱⲧⲉ ('redeem'). Parallel to ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' Identifies the Form of Light as the soul's redeemer — confirmed in apposition 'her redeemer who is the form of light' (line 21).

Possibly Greek ἀγάπη with anomalous ⲗ for ⲅ. Paired with ⲡⲁⲥⲡⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ ('kiss') in 'in unto the kiss with the embrace' — fits the standard liturgical pairing of kiss-of-peace and love-feast. Confidence low; awaiting parallels.
Greek loanword ἀσπασμός 'greeting, embrace, kiss.' Standard liturgical kiss-of-peace, here as one of the five sacramental signs. Translated 'kiss' to preserve the bodily-greeting register.
Greek loanword χειροτονία — formal ordination by stretching out / laying on of hands. The fifth sign in the Manichaean sequence; appropriate for catechumen-to-elect transition.
Greek loanword βραβεῖον — the victor's prize/wreath. Held by the angel who descends at the elect's death; the eschatological reward.
From Coptic ⲕⲗⲟⲙ 'crown, wreath' (Lyc ⲕⲗⲁⲙ). The crown of glory received in eternal life — a Manichaean and biblical commonplace.

proposed_english: the house of the Living Ones
rationale: ⲏⲓ̈ = ⲏⲓ 'house'; ⲛⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ = 'those who live, the Living Ones.' The heavenly abode from which the apostle's teaching has been brought. Cf. ⲡⲣⲕⲗⲏⲧⲟⲥ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ 'the Living Paraclete' — same root.
